building: Delta Zeta (Xi Omega Chapter), Purdue University
review_mode: independent read-only review of saved preview and recorded fresh-open evidence
key_strengths: Direct official GIS FID 752 identity and address evidence, with official chapter sources and dated supporting context.
Official 11-vertex GIS polygon defines the modeled wall-base ring; saved comparison reports 0.0000311 m max corner-to-vertex error, clearly qualified as same-source/by-construction.
Independent unnamed OSM ring provides a useful secondary general footprint check (IoU 0.893, Hausdorff 3.50 m, centroid offset 1.16 m) without being misrepresented as identity proof.
Entry composition and red brick align qualitatively with official Purdue photo description; cutaway is legible and correctly qualified as schematic.
Fresh-open report records stable one-object scene/collection, no external image datablocks, and no saved camera/light objects.
limitations: Exterior massing is still a simplified two-level brick block with a very broad, shallow pale-blue roof cap; roof profile/material and story count are not resolved by reliable architectural evidence. GIS reports one level, so the modeled two-level interpretation remains an estimate.
Facade rhythm is repetitive and window openings are generic. Available imagery supports brick and entry features but not exact window count, dimensions, floor heights, or elevations.
Render colors are clean and separable but the pale roof, blue cast/background, and stylized near-white trim reduce resemblance to the likely physical palette.
Interior room names are supported by the 2023 chapter feature, while room locations, partitions, dimensions, and furnishings are schematic and not current as-built evidence.
The GIS outline is not surveyed control; OSM differs by up to 3.50 m and 1.16 m centroid offset.
recommended_refinements: If another exterior source is found, refine roof slope/edge profile and facade proportions to match it; otherwise keep the roof explicitly labeled as an estimate.
Tune brick/roof colors toward the source photo and reduce the cool blue cast in the exterior preview.
Compare window spacing and door dimensions against a front elevation if one becomes available.
Keep the interior marked as schematic and avoid implying the labeled rooms are in measured positions.
